```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-studio-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The task</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Produce:</b> an audit note on a study that weighs cost against carbon: each flaw, its fix and its effect, then the corrected conclusion with the condition it rests on.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> a fictional study of 40 electric buses, its tables, and your browser's recomputation of every number after each fix.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> the rubric's bar for Consistent accounting and for Realism: one boundary, the emissions question named, who pays named, inputs' evidence status and a list of what is left out.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 35 minutes guided here, then about 90 minutes on your own:</p>
<ul class="lx-hint">
<li>pick a study from your field: a report, a paper or a press release;</li>
<li>run the checklist under Self-check on it;</li>
<li>recompute one number it rests on, on one boundary;</li>
<li>write the audit note and rate it against the rubric.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="r07-cost-carbon-properly" data-src="../assets/learn/data/r07-cost-carbon-properly.json ../assets/learn/data/path.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r07-task:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The study (fictional)</p>
<p><b>Electric buses for Port Alder: cheaper and carbon-free</b>. R. Okonjo and L. Varga, Harbourline Consulting (fictional), report to Port Alder Transit (fictional), 2026.</p>
<p>Replacing Port Alder Transit's 40 oldest diesel buses with battery-electric buses saves $1.15 million a year and cuts the fleet's CO₂ by 100%.</p>
<details class="lx-textalt"><summary>Four flaws, each fixed, and the conclusion after each</summary><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Fix</th><th scope="col">What it changes</th><th scope="col">Saving a year, electric against diesel</th><th scope="col">CO₂ cut</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>The study as published</td><td>none</td><td>$1.15 million</td><td>4,192 t (100%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>One boundary</td><td>One boundary: charging 3,168 MWh a year at 0.366 t per MWh emits 1,160 t. The CO₂ cut falls from 100% to 72%.</td><td>$1.15 million</td><td>3,033 t (72%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>A fair baseline</td><td>Fair baseline: new diesel buses burn 320,000 gallons a year, not 411,429. Diesel's yearly cost falls by $0.83 million.</td><td>$0.32 million</td><td>2,101 t (64%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Grid costs</td><td>Grid costs: $288,000 a year in demand charges, and $1.80 million up front for the depot ($180,832 a year as an annual equivalent).</td><td>−0.15 million</td><td>2,101 t (64%)</td></tr>
<tr><td>The credit once</td><td>The credit once: the $6.00 million stays off the price up front; the second count, $500,000 a year, goes.</td><td>−0.65 million</td><td>2,101 t (64%)</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div></details>
<p><b>Audited:</b> Electric costs $0.65 million a year more and cuts 2,101 t of CO₂ (64%): about $309 per tonne. That is for the transit agency, with the grid at EIA's 2023 U.S. average.</p>
<!-- r07-task:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you find each flaw, fix it and watch the conclusion change; your note stays in this browser.</p>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}

[4]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> No flaw is named, so no one can check or fix it.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> True at the tailpipe only; the power plants that charge them emit.</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> No number, no baseline, no 'whose cost'.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> It says nothing a reader could act on.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong note · Proficient</p><p class="lx-ex-lines">Boundary: charging is in the cost but its CO₂ is not; counted at EIA's 2023 U.S. average, the electric fleet emits 1,160 t a year. [1]
Baseline: without the project the agency buys new diesel buses (4.5 mpg), not the 2009 fleet (3.5 mpg). [2]
Grid: add the depot connection ($1.80 million up front) and demand charges ($288,000 a year). [3]
Credit: counted once, in the capital line; the second $500,000 a year removed. [4]
Conclusion: for the agency, electric costs $0.65 million a year more and cuts 2,101 t of CO₂ (64%), about $309 per tonne, if the grid is at the 2023 U.S. average. [5]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> Names the mismatch, the fix and the factor's source.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> The counterfactual, stated from the agency's own plan.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> Up front and annual kept apart.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> Says which count stays and why.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> Cost and CO₂ on one boundary, whose cost, and the condition that moves it most.</li></ol></div>
</div>

<p class="lx-eyebrow">Who pays, who gains: the audited plan, a year, against new diesel buses</p><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Who</th><th scope="col">Cost or change</th><th scope="col">Per tonne of CO₂ avoided</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Port Alder Transit<br><span class="lx-hint">the agency's budget</span></th><td>+$0.65 million a year</td><td>$309 per tonne (about)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">The state<br><span class="lx-hint">pays the credit</span></th><td>$6.00 million up front ($0.60 million a year as an annual equivalent)</td><td>a transfer to the agency</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Agency and state together<br><span class="lx-hint">the credit nets out</span></th><td>+$1.25 million a year</td><td>$595 per tonne (about)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">The climate<br><span class="lx-hint">CO₂, at EIA's 2023 U.S. grid average</span></th><td>−2,101 t a year</td><td>64% of the diesel fleet's</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Where the audited conclusion holds</p><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">It holds when</th><th scope="col">It leaves out</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><ul><li>the inputs are this fictional study's, in 2025 dollars, over a 12-year life at 3%;</li><li>charging's CO₂ is at the grid's average factor (EIA, 2023); a marginal factor for the hours buses charge could differ (A10);</li><li>the agency pays the depot connection; the state pays the credit once;</li><li>both fleets run the same routes and miles.</li></ul></td><td><ul><li>making the buses and batteries (a life-cycle boundary, A11);</li><li>tailpipe air pollution and noise in the streets, which electric buses cut;</li><li>a grid that gets cleaner over the 12 years, and battery replacement;</li><li>federal grants, fuel and power price changes.</li></ul></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">How far up the ladder is each number?</p><ul><li>The transit board voted the money for 40 electric buses. <b>Funded.</b> Funded: money committed, nothing built yet.</li><li>The utility approved the depot's new service connection. <b>Permitted.</b> Permitted: approved, not yet built; its cost estimate is still an estimate.</li><li>Ten electric buses have carried passengers since March. <b>Operating.</b> Operating: in service, but a few months do not show a year's energy use.</li><li>Over a full year the ten buses used their expected energy per mile, winter included. <b>At design output.</b> At design output: the 2.2 kWh per mile now rests on measured service, not a brochure.</li><li>The study's corrected cost per tonne of CO₂ avoided. <b>Not on the ladder: a projection.</b> A projection: a model's output from inputs on several rungs, not a stage of anything built.</li></ul>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Which grid factor, and which question?</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>The audit counts charging at the grid's average factor: the buses' share of what the plants emit.</li>
<li>What charging changes depends on which plants respond in the hours the buses charge, now and as the grid is built out: <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a>'s questions 2 and 3.</li>
<li>Name which question your number answers, and show the result at the other factors, as step 6 does.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this studio leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>A life-cycle boundary: making the buses and their batteries (<a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a>).</li>
<li>Health and noise in the streets, which electric buses improve.</li>
<li>Uncertainty in each input: <a href="r06-uncertainty-properly.html">R6</a>.</li>
<li>Who pays for a depot connection when a utility recovers it from all its customers: the cost moves, it does not vanish.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check your own work against the rubric
:::

```{=html}
<div id="r07-rubric" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r07-rubric:start (written by LX.Rubric's staticHTML, from the course rubric, and from the data file's checklist, in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts lx-rb-static"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Competence</th><th scope="col">Developing</th><th scope="col">Proficient (the bar)</th><th scope="col">Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Consistent accounting<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: cost and CO₂ on one boundary, the emissions question named (what changes against a stated counterfactual), and whose cost each number is.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Costs and emissions on different boundaries.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Cost and emissions on one boundary; emissions question named; who pays and who benefits named.</td><td data-l="Strong">Distributional and environmental side effects estimated with stated assumptions.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Realism<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: each key input with its evidence status, and a list of what the audit leaves out.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Assumes announced projects exist.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Evidence status of key inputs; a 'what the analysis leaves out' list.</td><td data-l="Strong">Realism checked with a practitioner or primary documents.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Cost and carbon, before you trust a result</p>
<ul><li><b>Same service:</b> Both options deliver the same service: the same routes and miles, the same years.</li><li><b>One boundary:</b> Everything inside the cost boundary is inside the CO₂ boundary, and the reverse; what is left out is said.</li><li><b>A stated counterfactual:</b> One sentence says what happens without the project, from a plan or a rule, not a convenient past.</li><li><b>The emissions question:</b> Average or marginal factor, and why: whose share, or what changes.</li><li><b>Grid and connection costs:</b> Upgrades, demand charges and connection fees are priced, with who pays them.</li><li><b>Credits once:</b> Each grant or credit appears in one line, and is a transfer for the state and the agency together.</li><li><b>Up front and annual apart:</b> One-time amounts and their annual equivalents are labelled, with the rate and the life.</li><li><b>The condition that moves it:</b> The input that changes the conclusion most is named, with the result at its other values.</li></ul>
<!-- r07-rubric:end -->
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="r7-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="tailpipe" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A fleet with no tailpipe emits no CO₂.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Charging Port Alder's buses at the 2023 U.S. average emits about 1,160 t a year at the power plants.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="credit" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A purchase credit makes a project cheaper for everyone.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It moves money from the state to the agency: the audited buses cost the agency $0.65 million a year more, and the two together $1.25 million.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="baseline" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The fair baseline is the fleet running today.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It is what would happen without the project: here the replacement plan's new diesel buses, not the 2009 ones.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>From this studio to your own study</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li><b>Proficient:</b> cost and CO₂ on one boundary, the emissions question named, who pays named, inputs' evidence status and what is left out.</li>
<li><b>Strong goes further:</b> side effects for other people and places, estimated with stated assumptions.</li>
<li><b>To test it:</b> give your note to someone who did not write the study, and ask them to recompute one number.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
